A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Mod-Adapter research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocation and reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original personalization experiments, component ablations, expert-utilization analysis, and a 32-participant user study, including Tables 1–3.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds expert-count and clustering experiments in Table 4 and k-means utilization results in Figure 6(c).

M1.justification: The proposed FLUX-based adapter, vision-language attention, 12-expert k-means routing, VLM-supervised pretraining, and training/inference procedures remain unchanged. Hierarchical clustering is evaluated as an ablation alternative, without replacing the proposed routing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use MVImgNet, AFHQ, and FLUX-generated abstract-concept training data, and evaluate single- and multi-concept personalization on DreamBench-Abs. Its 30 object/animal concepts, 20 abstract concepts, and 30 multi-concept combinations are retained. New ablations do not expand task or data coverage.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds hierarchical clustering as an evaluated alternative to the proposed k-means routing at 12 experts. The main benchmark, qualitative, and user-study comparators remain Emu2, MIP-Adapter, MS-Diffusion, and TokenVerse.

E3.justification: Appendix F introduces experiments varying expert counts across 1, 4, 8, and 12 and comparing clustering procedures. Existing benchmark settings, metrics, training budgets, and user-study design remain unchanged. The new train/test non-overlap statement documents the existing evaluation rather than establishing a changed split.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations, Table 4 tests sensitivity to expert count and clustering choice. Figure 6(c) adds direct evidence about utilization under k-means routing alongside the existing learned-gating analysis. These are focused extensions of the existing MoE investigation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The new experiments retain point-score reporting; expert-assignment percentages describe routing utilization rather than uncertainty.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–3 and the qualitative examples are retained. Table 4 newly reports multi-concept CP·PF scores of 0.22, 0.25, and 0.37 for 1, 4, and 8 experts, and 0.63 for hierarchical clustering versus the retained 12-expert k-means score of 0.62. Figure 6(c) adds utilization shares ranging from 6.7% to 11.1%.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6, including modulation directions, cross-attention, and the pretraining loss, retain the same mathematics. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and the additional clustering discussion introduces no new formal assumption or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: tuning-free object and abstract multi-concept personalization, Mod-Adapter, VLM-guided pretraining, DreamBench-Abs, and claimed superior performance. Added novelty adjectives and supporting experiments do not change these claims' scientific scope.

C2.justification: v3 explains the 12-expert choice through an 80GB memory constraint and discusses the overhead of scaling through CPU offloading. It also expands the explanation connecting TokenVerse's reconstruction-focused training to unseen-prompt performance. The repeated-concept-name and more-than-three-concept limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 newly states the 1,667.77M trainable parameter count, train/test image and prompt separation, and memory constraint. Existing optimizer, hardware, and training settings move to Appendix C. The project-page links are removed and a source-code release upon acceptance is promised; the PDFs do not establish an actual change in external availability.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds discussion and citations including P+, BLIP-Diffusion, BLIP-2, and EasyControl, with more explicit distinctions from single-concept methods and VLM-based pretraining. Some Custom Diffusion and DreamRelation exposition is removed while their citations remain. The central positioning relative to TokenVerse is retained.

P1.justification: v3 revises related-work paragraphs and selected explanations, moves the adapter discussion and implementation details into Appendices B and C, and updates affiliations, citation style, and cross-references. Most method, experiment, and conclusion prose retains its original organization and meaning.

P2.justification: A document-wide template change alters the title and author block, running headers, typography, heading styles, reference layout, and table sizing. Table 3 and Figure 5 are relocated, Table 4 is added, and Figure 6 is reformatted from two panels to three. Other figure content is retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix F strengthens support for the MoE design through expert-count and clustering tests and direct k-means utilization evidence. Added parameter, memory, and train/test separation disclosures improve transparency. These are limited gains because the principal results and failure conditions remain unchanged. Removing the project-page links weakens access guidance despite the new release-on-acceptance promise.
